findings.description: The DB username and password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local application configuration file. This exposes the credential to users or processes able to retrieve instance user data or read the created file.

`publicly_accessible = true` gives the RDS instance a public endpoint. The currently shown ingress is VPC-scoped, but assigning public reachability unnecessarily expands the database attack surface and makes its isolation wholly dependent on security-group controls.
`storage_encrypted = false` leaves RDS storage, including database data and automated backups where applicable, unencrypted at rest.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports to `0.0.0.0/0`. A compromised database host can make unrestricted outbound connections, defeating network-segmentation controls.

The EC2-assumable application role permits `s3:*`, `ec2:*`, and `rds:*` on every resource. Since it is attached to `catalog_app_server`, compromise of that instance grants broad account control and data-access capabilities, including likely privilege-escalation paths.
